outcome: Cohen, Pohoata and Zakharov improved the upper bound for the Heilbronn triangle problem from Δ(n) ≤ n^(-8/7-1/2000) (their own 2023, pre-window result) to Δ(n) ≤ n^(-7/6+o(1)), first posted as arXiv:2409.07658 'Lower bounds for incidences' in September 2024 and now accepted at Inventiones Mathematicae; the lower bound (Komlós–Pintz–Szemerédi, 1982) has not moved in the window, and the general asymptotic problem remains open.
summary: The bullet asks for movement on either bound of the Heilbronn triangle problem: the largest known lower-bound construction and the smallest known upper bound on the maximum guaranteed empty-triangle area Δ(n) for n points in the unit square. The upper bound moved in the window. Cohen, Pohoata and Zakharov's May 2023 paper (arXiv:2305.18253, pre-window) had given Δ(n) ≤ n^(-8/7-1/2000), the first improvement in 40 years over Komlós–Pintz–Szemerédi (1981/82). Their follow-up 'Lower bounds for incidences' (arXiv:2409.07658, v1 11 Sep 2024, v2 18 Mar 2025, now published in Inventiones Mathematicae) proves the sharper upper bound Δ(n) ≤ n^(-7/6+o(1)) by establishing a new incidence bound between points and tubes; this attains what the authors call the 'high-low limit' of their method, i.e. a natural barrier for the current approach. This is squarely the quantity named in the bullet and is well past preprint into expert digestion (Inventiones acceptance, a University of Pennsylvania harmonic-analysis seminar talk by Cohen in Jan 2025, a Wikipedia lead that now states this as the state of the art), so I classified the September 2024 posting as the dated event and used the improvement itself — a bound moving on a problem that remains open — as `progress` rather than `resolved`, since the general problem (closing the gap between n^-2 and n^(-7/6+o(1))) is untouched. No source, including the Quanta profile of the 2023 result, the seminar-talk abstract, or the papers themselves, attributes any part of the mathematics to an AI system; the work is described throughout as a fusion of Roth's classical approach with recent harmonic-analysis/fractal-geometry incidence estimates, done by hand. I also checked adjacent Heilbronn-adjacent work for scope and AI relevance: Zakharov's 2024 higher-dimensional-Heilbronn paper and the October 2025 Maldague–Wang–Zakharov 3D Heilbronn paper (arXiv:2510.26644) are variants over different ambient spaces, not cases of this 2D bullet, and report no AI use. A May 2024 k-gons paper (arXiv:2405.12945) is about k≥4-gons, a different (related) problem, not this one. Gabor Ellmann's long-running preprint (arXiv:1703.03297, originally 2017, revised repeatedly through November 2025) gives an explicit lower-bound construction on a unit circle with bound Ω(n^-1.5 (log n)^-7/2); this construction predates the frozen revision (v1, 2017) and its exponent appears unchanged through the in-window revisions I could inspect (v6, Feb 2024, states the same O(n^-1.5(log n)^-7/2)), so I did not treat it as an in-window change to the lower bound, though I could not fully diff every revision's full text. Two December 2025/2026 computational papers (arXiv:2512.14505, and arXiv:2603.11107 'From Computational Certification to Exact Coordinates') use Gurobi mixed-integer optimization and Gröbner-basis symbolic computation to pin down exact optimal configurations for small n (5-9 points); these are a different, discrete/exact-optimization case of the problem (not the asymptotic bound the bullet is about) and explicitly use no machine learning or AI, only classical solvers and computer algebra.
competing_reading: One could argue the 2023 n^(-8/7-1/2000) paper and the 2024/2025 n^(-7/6+o(1)) paper are really one continuous program, in which case the 'event' could instead be dated to the 2023 preprint (pre-window, making this open_stale) with the 2024 paper as a mere refinement worth mentioning only in summary. I rejected this because the two papers state numerically and qualitatively different bounds, the second was posted and published entirely within the window, and the seminar/Wikipedia treatment of the two as separate results supports treating the September 2024 posting as its own event.
what_would_settle_it: Confirmation from the Inventiones publication record of the exact acceptance/publication date, and a full read of all Ellmann revision diffs (2017-2025) to be certain no in-window revision changed the exponent on the lower-bound side.
